subject: science
source: CISCE Curriculum for Primary Classes I-V (2016), official

covers: Name the food items a family uses, on ordinary days and on special occasions
Sort food by its job: energy, body building and protection from disease
Name the components of food: carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water and roughage
Explain in their own words why a balanced diet matters
Explain why children, adults and elders need different amounts and kinds of food
Suggest ways to avoid wasting food
Name the kinds of teeth and where they sit in the mouth
Draw a tooth and label its parts, and say what each kind of tooth does
Compare the number of teeth in infants and adults
Give reasons why teeth and gums get damaged
Suggest ways to keep teeth and gums healthy: brushing, healthy food and regular check-ups
Understand what causes cavities and how to prevent them

topics.topic: Human Body: The Digestive and Excretory Systems
covers: Name the organs of the digestive system and say what each one does
Name the organs of the excretory system and say what each one does
Explain why chewing food well helps digestion
Explain why water is needed for digestion and for removing wastes
Explain why regular bowel movements matter
List habits that keep the digestive and excretory organs healthy
Explain why animals need adaptations to survive in their habitats
Give examples of adaptations for life on land and in water
Link the body parts of herbivores, carnivores and omnivores with what they eat
Give examples of animals in each of these three food groups
Show care and concern for animals
Explain why plants need adaptations to survive in their habitat
Give examples of plant adaptations on land, in water, in deserts and in hilly areas
Draw pictures of different plant adaptations

topics.topic: Plants in the Surroundings and Environment
covers: Classify plants as herbs, shrubs and trees
Identify tap roots and fibrous roots, and give examples of plants with each
Describe the work of the stem and the leaf in simple words
Explain photosynthesis and transpiration in simple, non-technical words
Use a hand lens to find stomata on a leaf
Show that a leaf has starch, using the iodine test, with help from elders
Name plant products such as wood, coir, rubber and fibres, and their uses
Show that air has weight, takes up space and expands when heated
Name the parts of air: gases and water vapour
Explain breathing and burning in simple words
Name the causes of air pollution, such as dust, smoke, spitting and germs
Suggest ways to keep the air clean
Explain solvent, solute and solution, with everyday examples
Tell soluble and insoluble substances apart, in water and in oil
Make solutions using different solvents
Separate solid from liquid by sedimentation, decantation, filtration and evaporation
Give an example of each separation method, such as sand in water and sugar in water
Name natural and artificial sources of light
Tell luminous objects from non-luminous objects
Tell transparent, translucent and opaque objects apart, with examples
Explain in simple language how a shadow is formed
Appreciate how natural light is used in daily life
Find ways to save light energy
Explain why we need units to measure things
Name measuring instruments: scale, tape, weighing machine, ruler, thermometer and clock
Say what each instrument measures, and how to read and use it
Give everyday examples where measuring is needed, such as buying goods or telling time
Tell push and pull apart, with examples
Explain that a force can change the shape or direction of an object
Name the forces met in daily life: muscular, gravitational, magnetic and frictional
Explain each force in their own words, with a daily-life example
Show push and pull in group activities, with safety in mind
Explain friction in their own words, with examples from daily life
Name the uses of friction, such as grip for walking and for stopping
Name the harmful effects of friction
Show how oil or powder reduces friction
Carry out simple activities that show friction on different surfaces
